name: HiSilicon Kirin 950 mobile system-on-chip
description: HiSilicon combined four Arm Cortex-A72 and four Cortex-A53 cores, a Mali-T880 MP4 GPU and an LTE modem in its Kirin 950 (Hi3650) mobile system-on-chip. TSMC made the chip on 16FF+ for use in the Huawei Mate 8.

date.label: 5 November 2015
date.basis: Same-day coverage dates the public press presentation in Beijing.

events.statement: Huawei presented HiSilicon’s Kirin 950 at a press event in Beijing where it showed the chip running on a reference platform.

evidence.locator: Dated byline, opening paragraphs and paragraph on the reference platform
evidence.supports: The report dates the briefing and describes the reference-platform demonstration.

evidence.locator: 关键特性 [Key specifications], Process, CPU, GPU and Modem
evidence.supports: The chip designer identifies the chip, its parts and its process.

date.label: 26 November 2015
date.basis: The Paper’s contemporary on-site report dates the event to 26 November.

events.statement: Huawei presented the Mate 8 incorporating the Kirin 950 at the Shanghai World Expo Center.
events.scope: Presentation of the handset with the SoC.

evidence.locator: Opening photograph caption and event account; discussion of the Kirin 950
evidence.supports: The event account dates and locates the unveiling. Huawei’s CEO identifies the Kirin 950 used in the phone.

date.label: 9 December 2015
date.basis: Huawei’s January 2016 release gives the date on which Chinese sales began.

events.statement: The Huawei Mate 8 went on sale in China with the Kirin 950.
events.scope: Handset offered for sale in China.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph on 9 December sales; paragraph comparing Chinese and overseas configurations
evidence.supports: Gives the Chinese retail sale date and names the Kirin 950 in the handset.
The 24 December disassembly independently locates a Kirin 950 package in a Mate 8 handset.
Independently identifies the Hi3650 die in a Mate 8. The analysis report was published later and does not date the sale.

earliest_record.rationale: The first dated public product milestone retained is the 5 November press presentation.

unresolved.note: The public physical-analysis synopsis identifies the Mate 8 model. Its regional SKU, wafer lot and fabrication site are unreported. The separately dated foundry ramp applies to the process as a whole.

links.statement: TSMC’s 16FF+ process fabricated the HiSilicon Kirin 950 used in the Huawei Mate 8.
links.scope: The Hi3650 die in the Huawei Mate 8 model confirmed by physical analysis.

evidence.locator: 关键特性 [Key specifications], Process, CPU, GPU and Modem
evidence.supports: HiSilicon explicitly specifies TSMC 16nm FF+ for the SoC.
TechInsights independently identifies TSMC 16FF+ FinFET CMOS in the extracted Hi3650 die.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph on 9 December sales; paragraph comparing Chinese and overseas configurations
evidence.supports: Huawei identifies the Kirin 950 on FinFET+ in the commercially sold Mate 8.
